scope: Core personal notification subscription authorization and Header WS lifecycle

initial_report.source: user supplied AI Craft feedback, historical Safari session not directly observed

root_causes: Production DefaultAuthorizer required an exact member Topic ACL for personal notifications, while Root bypassed that check. Existing receipt/WS tests supplied an always-allow ACL and missed this.
WS module-global initialized flags outlived the first component scope that owned identity watches. New sessions with the same token were not independently observed.
Header needed to wait for the current session member context and track an already-open shared socket when context became ready later.
fixes: Only canonical registered _topic.system.notification subscribe uses verified JWT plus live IAM member identity; publish/replay and other topics keep existing ACL rules.
Hub target filtering and live write-time tenant/member/JWT validation remain enforced; revoked identities close their sockets.
Per-consumer watches, auth/storage/network listeners and subscriptions are released with their Vue scope; the last subscription closes the shared socket.
Header waits for a matching session context, rejects stale callbacks, synchronizes read receipts through existing Pinia store and refreshes once on reconnect.
No periodic notification status/list reads, no new contract/table/migration, no Framework/plugin edits.

reproduction_before_fix.frontend: WS lifecycle suite: 3 of 4 tests failed, covering scope remount and same-token new local/storage sessions
reproduction_before_fix.backend: Real WS fixture with production authorizer and denied member ACL received error instead of subscribe ack

includes: bell 2 to 1 while old notice remains unread

multiple consumers release only owned subscriptions
signed service token to actual HTTP receipt route to DB to member WS

intermediate_failures: After introducing live IAM into authorizer, revoked write test exposed an early return before socket cleanup; canDeliver now also checks recipient identity on authorization failure and the race test passes.

HTTP test compilation temporarily failed on an unrelated concurrently edited recovery dependency (undefined recoveryops, then import cycle); this task did not modify that module. Current source passed HTTP tests, vet and full app build.
Extended shared-socket reconnect coverage required updating the older mock to model the transport dropping the old session socket during identity changes; final frontend suite passed all 30 tests.
